subject: EU edge deployment — training assurances & deletion propagation
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@novushealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Clarification request — training guarantees and data deletion for EU edge

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed with the PoC on your EU-edge offering, our security team asked a couple of concrete things I couldn't answer off the top of my head. Could you confirm the following?

1) Do you ever use customer request payloads (text, attachments, metadata) to train or fine-tune any Redwood models (including internal research variants)?
2) For the EU-edge/private deployment, where is ephemeral state (KV cache, session context) stored? Is it ever persisted to disk/backups that might leave the EU region?
3) What is your retention SLA for request logs, debug traces, and audit logs for hosted versus private deployments? Can we request an immediate purge for a customer?

We need written confirmations we can include with our DPA sign-off and the audit intake. If convenient, please attach your DPA/SOC2 evidence and the architecture diagram for the EU-edge.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Security, Novus Health
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@novushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 10:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarification request — training guarantees and data deletion for EU edge

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we do not train on customer request data by default; EU-edge keeps customer data in-region; and we expose a deletion API for expedited removals. Details below and attaching our DPA.

Attachment: DataProcessingAddendum.pdf (PDF)

Details:
- Training usage: Redwood's hosted and private offerings do not use customer input to train or fine-tune public models. We maintain separation between serving data and downstream model training workflows. Any research use of telemetry is done on aggregated, anonymized metrics and only with Legal/Customer opt-in.

- Telemetry and operational logs: by default, ephemeral request traces and KV cache keys used to accelerate inference are retained for SLO/debugging and quality monitoring. For Hosted EU-edge (managed by Redwood in EU regions) default retention for these traces is 30 days. Billing records (token counts, invoice metadata) are retained per our billing policy and are pseudonymized for 13 months for accounting.

- Private / VPC deployments: customers can opt to disable telemetry collection at provisioning time. For on-prem or fully air-gapped installs, no telemetry leaves the customer's network unless explicitly enabled.

- Deletion options: we provide a programmatic deletion endpoint (/v1/customers/{customer_id}/data-delete) which issues an async purge request. For hosted EU-edge we aim for deletion propagation to all cache layers and auditing backends within 24-72 hours; archives (if any) are removed per the retention window in the DPA unless a longer legal hold applies.

Next steps: Monica (cc'd) can provide the EU-edge architecture diagram and the SOC2 redacted report. If you want a shorter retention window for the PoC we can set the trace retention to 7 days for the trial.

Best,
Logan Wright
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@novushealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Novus Health Security Team <security@novushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 08:43:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarification request — training guarantees and data deletion for EU edge

Logan — thanks, that's helpful. A couple of clarifying follow-ups from our infra team:

- KV cache: is it only in-memory (GPU/host memory) or do you ever spill to disk for long running sessions? If spills/backups exist, are they encrypted and stored in EU buckets?
- Backups/archives: you mentioned "archives (if any)" above. For hosted EU-edge — do you create nightly backups that are kept longer than the trace retention window? If so, where are they stored and how are they deleted?
- Deletion API: does it support a synchronous verification token we can include in our audit evidence (i.e., a request id + completion timestamp)?

If you can confirm the KV behavior and backup lifecycle we can move forward with the DPA review. Also, please flag any actions that require Legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Samantha
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@novushealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 14:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Clarification request — training guarantees and data deletion for EU edge

Hi Samantha — happy to dive in with more technical specifics. I'm including Karthik from Product infra for the backup details. See answers below and I've attached a simple diagram of the EU-edge layout.

Attachment: eu-edge-architecture-diagram.png (image)

Technical details:
- KV cache behavior: primary KV cache is in-memory on the inference host (GPU RAM / host RAM). We do not persist KV cache to long-term object storage by default. For long-running sessions that request checkpointing (explicitly enabled by the customer for session resume), a checkpoint blob may be written to an encrypted EU-only object store. Those checkpoint blobs are created only with explicit customer consent and are tied to the customer tenant; they are encrypted with customer-managed keys if requested.

- Backups/archives: Redwood does not create rolling nightly backups of raw request payloads for Hosted EU-edge. Operational snapshots (for disaster recovery) are taken at the service level but do not contain identifiable request payloads — they contain configuration and software state. Any persistent customer artifacts (checkpoints, uploaded attachments stored for your application) are kept per the DPA. For Hosted EU-edge we do keep redacted debugging archives for severe incident analysis; those are time-limited and retained for up to 90 days and stored in EU-only buckets with server-side encryption.

- Deletion API and evidence: the deletion API returns an async request id and emits a completion event with a timestamp you can fetch via /v1/customers/{id}/data-delete/status. We also generate a signed audit record (JSON) that includes the purge request id, affected data categories, and a completion timestamp suitable for compliance evidence. If you need a certificate-style attestation, Legal can produce a signed confirmation for one-off purges (requires justification).

Legal/Compliance notes:
- Anything beyond the standard DPA terms (e.g., shorter retention windows globally or wholesale disabling of certain telemetry across Redwood's hosted fleet) will require Legal engagement and may impact billing/SLA.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your team if you want to walk this through.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Principal Product Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
